strengths: Strong empirical results surpassing GPT-4o on average across 8 diverse benchmarks (55.82% vs 53.20%)
Comprehensive experimental evaluation with thorough ablation studies, learning curves, and qualitative analysis demonstrating the approach's effectiveness
Well-motivated problem identification showing complementary strengths/weaknesses of different reasoning modes with intuitive solution
Technically sound approach with elegant mode unification via prefix tokens and well-justified AdaGRPO algorithm components
Good reproducibility with detailed implementation details, hyperparameters, and promised open-source release
weaknesses: Critical fairness issue: fallback mode-switching mechanism during evaluation provides unfair advantage unavailable to single-mode baselines, undermining comparison validity and suggesting adaptive selection mechanism may be unreliable
Significant gap to upper bound (e.g., 50.8% vs 56.8% for AdaVaR-3B) reveals substantial room for improvement in core contribution; paper acknowledges but provides no concrete solutions
Limited to demonstrating only two reasoning modes despite claims of extensibility; generalizability to other mode combinations unclear
Moderate technical novelty—combining multiple modes is sensible but incremental; RL for mode selection follows established patterns without fundamental innovation

Complex data construction using auxiliary models (GPT-4o, Qwen2.5-VL-72B) with rejection sampling makes exact reproduction difficult; high computational cost (32 A100 GPUs × 29h) not discussed or compared to baselines
Inadequate analysis of mode selection failure modes; no systematic breakdown of when/why adaptive selection fails; no error-type analysis or confidence-correctness correlation

No statistical significance testing despite small performance margins (1-2 percentage points); SFT stage shows poor mode selection (31% grounding preference despite text superiority) but limited exploration of alternatives

strengths: Well-motivated problem identifying complementary strengths of text-based vs visually-grounded reasoning modes across domains
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across 8 diverse benchmarks with consistent improvements (AdaVaR-7B surpasses GPT-4o on average)
Extensive analysis including mode selection behavior, error categorization, training dynamics, and ablation studies
Clear technical framework with sensible two-stage training design (SFT then RL) and elegant mode unification via prefix tokens
Strong reproducibility with detailed hyperparameters, training procedures, and promise to open-source code/models
Thorough appendix with supplementary experiments, qualitative analysis, and implementation details
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: AdaGRPO modifications are incremental (prefix-guided exploration simply fixes mode prefix; mode-relative advantage uses standard Gaussian assumption; curriculum learning is well-established)

Evaluation concerns: (1) ad-hoc mode-switching mechanism when model gets stuck in repetitive logic could artificially inflate performance; (2) data construction uses GPT-4o reformatting and distillation from another VLM (Orsta) raising data independence questions; (3) no statistical significance testing or error bars reported; (4) some improvements modest (e.g., +1.5% on POPE)
Significant gap to upper bound on several benchmarks (e.g., MathVista: 69.8 vs 74.8 for AdaVaR-3B) with limited investigation into why mode selection remains suboptimal
Limited scope restricted to 2 reasoning modes; scalability to 3+ modes not demonstrated despite claims about paradigm generalizability
Mostly descriptive rather than mechanistic analysis of mode selection (e.g., why 51% grounded on MMStar vs 2% on MathVista?); limited investigation of root causes for selection patterns
Generalization concerns: limited to English, unclear extension to other modalities, data efficiency moderate (384K vs 1.8M for LLaVA-OV)
Missing comparisons with simpler test-time ensemble approaches and other adaptive/mixture-of-experts methods in vision

strengths: Clear problem motivation with well-demonstrated complementary strengths of text-based vs. visually-grounded reasoning modes
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across 8 diverse benchmarks with extensive baseline comparisons and thorough ablations
Strong empirical results: AdaVaR-7B surpasses GPT-4o on average; consistent improvements across all benchmarks for 7B model
Elegant technical design with unified prefix-based mode representation enabling natural mode control
Exemplary reproducibility with complete prompts, detailed hyperparameters, and comprehensive supplementary materials
Deep analysis of learned behavior including fine-grained mode selection, attention visualization, and error categorization
Well-structured writing with effective presentation and clear problem formulation
weaknesses: Limited algorithmic novelty: prefix-based control, Gaussian-based advantage calculation, and GRPO adaptation are incremental; contribution primarily in engineering rather than novel algorithms
Scope restricted to two reasoning modes only; claims about 'general visual reasoning' limited; width/depth extensions theoretical rather than empirical
Mode-switching mechanism lacks quantitative analysis; appears to provide AdaVaR advantages unavailable to baselines, raising evaluation fairness concerns
Significant gap to oracle upper bound (MathVista: 69.8 vs 74.8; MathVision: 24.5 vs 30.9) suggests fundamental mode selection limitations
Mode selection mechanism concerns: attention analysis shows 97% weight on text tokens vs. 3% on images, suggesting visual information underutilized and mode selection primarily text-driven
Limited theoretical justification for design choices: why is mode-relative advantage via Gaussian CDF optimal? Curriculum strategy appears ad-hoc
Generalization unvalidated: all experiments on Qwen2.5-VL base model only; no evidence of transfer to other LVLMs
Marginal improvements on some benchmarks and lack of statistical significance testing undermine some performance claims
